title: Singleton mass under a product measure
statement: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be measurable spaces, let $\mu_1$ be a measure on $\alpha$, and let $\mu_2$ be a sigma-finite measure on $\beta$. For every $x\in\alpha$ and $y\in\beta$, the real-valued measure of the singleton $\{(x,y)\}$ under the product measure is the product of its real-valued singleton measures: $(\mu_1\otimes\mu_2)(\{(x,y)\})=\mu_1(\{x\})\mu_2(\{y\})$.
replaced:
Let $\mu_1$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and $\mu_2$ a $\sigma$-finite
measure on a measurable space $\beta$. Then for every $x \in \alpha$ and $y \in \beta$,
the real-valued mass that the product measure $\mu_1 \otimes \mu_2$ assigns to the
singleton $\{(x,y)\}$ is the product of the singleton masses:
\[
(\mu_1 \otimes \mu_2)(\{(x,y)\}) = \mu_1(\{x\})\,\mu_2(\{y\}).
\]
